metadata.note: The Western New York and Pennsylvania -- the Rochester-to-Emporium main line through the Genesee Valley and the Pennsylvania oil country. The company was incorporated in 1887 from the reorganization of the Buffalo, New York and Philadelphia Railroad, a 586-mile system, and was itself reorganized as the Western New York and Pennsylvania Railway in 1895. North of Hinsdale it ran on the Genesee Valley Canal Railroad of 1882, laid largely along the bed of the Genesee Valley Canal that New York State had abandoned in 1878 -- which is why the route hugs the river so closely and why the corridor survives today as the Genesee Valley Greenway. Unable to cover its bond interest, the WNY&P agreed on August 1 1900 to be operated by the Pennsylvania Railroad, becoming the PRR's Buffalo and Allegheny Valley Division, with the northern half worked as the Rochester Branch. Passenger service between Rochester and Olean ended in 1941; the corporate shell was merged into the Penndel Company in 1955 and the Rochester-Hinsdale line was abandoned in 1963. Two features share one geometry, split at the 1900 change of operator per CLAUDE.md Rule 4. NOT this railroad: the modern Western New York & Pennsylvania Railroad, a short line running over part of the same territory since 2001 -- it is a freight carrier, which CLAUDE.md Rule 1 keeps off this map.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_New_York_and_Pennsylvania_Railway (incorporated 1887 from the reorganization of the Buffalo, New York, and Philadelphia Railroad; reorganized 1895 as the Western New York and Pennsylvania Railway; system of 586.145 miles; main line from Emporium, Pennsylvania across the state line to Olean, Hinsdale, Cuba, Belfast and Rochester, the section from Belfast north laid on the bed of the abandoned Genesee Valley Canal; from 1895 to 1899 the company drew too little revenue to pay the bond interest; agreed to be operated by the PRR August 1 1900; became the PRR's Buffalo and Allegheny Valley Division; merged into the Penndel Company in 1955)

https://www.abandonedrails.com/genesee-valley-canal-railroad and https://nyrails.org/railroads/pennsylvania-railroad/hinsdale-rochester-line/ (Genesee Valley Canal Railroad opened 1882 from Rochester to Hinsdale near Olean, connecting to the Buffalo, New York and Philadelphia Railway; canal abandoned 1878; under the PRR the line was the Rochester Branch; passenger service between Rochester and Olean discontinued in 1941; six passenger trains and six to eight freight trains a day at its height; route abandoned 1963, now the Genesee Valley Greenway)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-08-24), two bbox queries covering Rochester to Emporium, assembled by corridor-constrained shortest path through geocoded waypoints (Rochester, Scottsville, Mount Morris, Nunda, Portageville, Fillmore, Belfast, Belvidere, Cuba, Hinsdale, Olean, Portville, Eldred, Port Allegany, Keating Summit, Emporium). Checked clean by the place-anchor artifact detector. See geometry_quality on each feature.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Whether PRR passenger service on the Olean-Emporium half (the Buffalo Line) continued past the 1941 Rochester-Olean discontinuance -- it very likely did, but no date was found, so the whole traced route ends at 1941 rather than asserting service on the northern half that had stopped. Headways before and after the 'six trains a day at its height' figure. The WNY&P's other 586-mile-system lines -- the Buffalo and Oil City routes among them -- are not traced here, only the Rochester-Emporium main line.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap by shortest path constrained to a 6 km corridor through the line's documented towns, with ways tagged old_railway_operator=PRR (and the Genesee Valley Greenway, Rochester Branch and Buffalo Line names) weighted in preference. 2523 points over 256.2 km (159.2 miles); 94.2% of that length sits on PRR or ex-PRR ways. The remainder is terminal and junction trackage the route shares with others -- 5.6 km on B&O ways, 2.8 km on NYC ways, and short unattributed pieces -- plus four straight links bridging gaps between abandoned fragments, the largest 1.34 km.

segments.note: Incorporated in 1887 out of the reorganization of the Buffalo, New York and Philadelphia Railroad, taking over a system of 586 miles. North of Hinsdale the route ran over the Genesee Valley Canal Railroad, opened in 1882 from Rochester to Hinsdale and laid largely on the bed of the Genesee Valley Canal, which had been abandoned in 1878. Six passenger trains a day ran on the Rochester-Olean section at its height, which is the basis for this 240-minute headway; the split between eras is estimated.
